Items.Authors: Bennet Schwab, Travis Curtis, Oswald Siegmund, Jason McPhate, Anton Tremsin
Items.Title: Design and test results of 50mm microchannel plate sealed tube detector for UV sounding rocket mission
Items.Abstract: New developments are presented on sealed tube microchannel plate detectors for two sounding rocket missions. This sensor is a hermetically sealed planacon tube with a proximity focused fused silica window and semitransparent bialkali photocathode. It combines a pair of 10-micron pore, 60:1 L/d, MgO Atomic Layer Deposited borosilicate microchannel plates with a high-resolution cross-strip anode. A novel external board converts the output of the cross strip anode into a cross delay line anode, simplifying the detectors on-board electrical interface while achieving the mission’s science-based performance requirements. This configuration is tailored for high efficiency imaging of far- and lyman-ultraviolet wavelengths with high resolution and low noise. Current testing meets the performance requirements of better than 100-micron spatial resolution. This detector will fly as part of two sounding rocket missions called FLUID and MOBIUS at the Laboratory of Atmospheric and Space Physics.

Items.Authors: Diane Chapuis Kerouanton, Gloria Mellinand, Malak Galal, Axel Nicolier, Aurélien Genin, Sébastien Pernecker, Rémi Giroud, Alexandre Jeanneau, Florence Laurent, Johan Richard, Jean-Paul Kneib, Zeno Amann
Items.Title: Design and testing of the motorized 2-DoF folding mirror 1 for the VLT BlueMUSE instrument
Items.Abstract: BlueMUSE is a blue-optimized, medium spectral resolution, panoramic integral field spectrograph under development for the Very Large Telescope (VLT). The project is now fully entering design phase. With an optimized transmission down to 350 nm, spectral resolution of R~3500 on average across the wavelength range, and a large FoV (1 arcmin²), BlueMUSE will open up a new range of galactic and extragalactic science cases facilitated by its specific capabilities.  In this paper, we present the design, implementation and evaluation of the motorized mount developed for Folding Mirror 1 (FM1) of the VLT BlueMUSE instrument. The mount provides two degrees of freedom in tip and tilt and is engineered to correct misalignments caused by environmental variations. The preliminary results demonstrate that the motorized FM1 tilt mount achieves the required precision and maintains alignment stability within the tight tolerances defined by the BlueMUSE project.

Items.Authors: Alicia M. Anderson, Samantha J. Thompson, Eugene B. Seneta, Alireza Esmaeilzadeh, Clark E. Baker, John S. Young, René Tronsgaard
Items.Title: Design and verification of the HARPS3 exposure meter: a dual-band photometer for improved photon-weighted barycentric correction
Items.Abstract: The High Accuracy Radial velocity Planet Searcher – 3 (HARPS3) is being developed for the Terra Hunting Experiment, a 10-year program targeting nightly observations of solar-like stars to search for long-period, low-mass exoplanets. Achieving 10 cm s⁻¹ radial-velocity precision requires accurate barycentric corrections, which depend on the true photon-weighted time of observation. Long exposures and CCD readout constraints make this difficult, so real-time flux monitoring is needed. Because atmospheric transmission varies across the optical range, the photon-weighted mid-time can differ for blue and red wavelengths. To account for this, we have designed a dual-band exposure meter for HARPS3 using a 550 nm dichroic to measure blue and red flux independently. We present the design, laboratory verification, and preliminary commissioning results of this new photometer, and discuss future plans for system characterisation with the HARPS3 spectrograph.

Items.Authors: Hangxin Ji, Xiaoyu Pan, Haoran Yu, Zhen Tang, Lei Wang, Jinhu Lv, Yong Li, Jun Li
Items.Title: Design considerations and trade-offs for a high-sensitivity UV-extended high-resolution echelle spectrograph (HEXIE) for the MOST telescope
Items.Abstract: The MOST Telescope is a new-generation optical facility designed for time-domain astronomy. To fully exploit its scientific potential, a High-sEnsitivity UV-eXtended hIgh-resolution Echelle spectrograph (HEXIE) is under development, enabling precise magnetic-field measurements and time-resolved polarimetry, and providing complementary coverage to ESPaDOnS and NARVAL. The instrument features 340–1050 nm spectral coverage, a spectral resolving power of R ∼ 77,000, high UV throughput, and excellent instrumental stability. A comprehensive optical trade-off study was performed, examining image-slicer configurations, main/cross-dispersion combinations, and camera/detector matching schemes. Despite potential structural benefits, image slicers were rejected due to UV throughput loss and increased system complexity. The final design adopts a mosaic R 2.9 echelle grating, a prism cross-disperser, and an F/2.5 UV-optimized camera matched to a deep depletion 4K CCD.

Items.Authors: Jialin Zhang, Jin Xu, Liubin Zhai, Bozhong Gu, Xiang Jiang, Ping Chen, Fujia Du
Items.Title: Design of a heavy-load field derotator structure and control system for large-aperture alt-azimuth astronomical telescopes
Items.Abstract: We present the mechanical and control design of a heavy-load field derotation system for a future 10 m class Chinese ground-based telescope. The derotator uses a 4.2 m diameter, 25 t capacity turntable with a large angular-contact bearing, torque-motor drive, and an absolute encoder with milliarcsecond-level resolution to provide high-stiffness, high-precision angular positioning. A two-mass model with a cascaded position-velocity-torque control architecture is implemented on a UMAC controller and tuned in the frequency domain to achieve a position loop bandwidth of 1.2–1.3 Hz while avoiding structural resonances. Simulations show smooth tracking with overshoot below 3%, satisfying stringent field rotation compensation requirements.

Items.Authors: Yi Meng, Hong-fei Zhang, Zong-wu He, Shi-hao Lu, Jian Wang
Items.Title: Design of a low-jitter pulse delay generator for astronomical gated cameras
Items.Abstract: Gated cameras are critical instruments for high-temporal-resolution observations in astronomy, widely used in fields such as high-resolution imaging of celestial bodies and laser guide star applications. To achieve precise gating control, the pulse delay generators driving the gating operation must possess picosecond-level delay precision. This paper presents the design and implementation of a high-precision, low-jitter pulse delay generator. The proposed hybrid delay architecture addresses the limitations of single-delay solutions in balancing precision and range: a coarse delay with a 5 ns step is implemented using a Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA), while a fine delay step of 10.07 ps is achieved with a dedicated delay chip (NB6L295MMNG). Test results demonstrate that the prototype exhibits a timing jitter as low as 11.3382 ps, with a standard deviation of 0.3622 ps, indicating excellent timing stability.

Items.Authors: Qihang Zhang, Yi Wu, Shuangquan Chen, Yonggang Gu, Chao Zhai
Items.Title: Design of the positioning robot's sensorless closed-loop drive system for LAMOST
Items.Abstract: LAMOST is currently undergoing renovation. To further enhance observational efficiency, a novel integrated fiber positioning robot has been designed, driven by a 4mm miniature hollow cup motor to control three times the number of fibers within the same space. Most such miniature motors employ open-loop control. To further improve positioning accuracy and controllability, we propose a closed-loop control scheme based on sensorless position sensing. This paper details the design of the fiber positioning robot's drive system, focusing on its software and hardware components. It covers communication protocols, closed-loop algorithms, and mechanical structures. Testing was conducted on a pilot platform with visual feedback to validate fiber positioning accuracy. Experimental results confirm that this drive system achieves significantly improved positioning accuracy compared to open-loop control, providing a more efficient and precise control solution for fiber positioning.

Items.Authors: Nicholas MacDonald, Jean-Thomas Landry, Marc-Andre Boucher, William Deich, Daren Dillon, Michael Gonzales, Renata Kupke, Dale Sandford, Andy Skemer, Deno Stelter
Items.Title: Design, fabrication, and testing of the SCALES dispersion carousel and optical mounts
Items.Abstract: The SCALES instrument, planned for deployment in 2026 on the Keck II telescope, employs a 14-position carousel to position dispersive elements at the spectrograph pupil. Operating over the 2–5 µm wavelength range, SCALES provides multiple spectral passbands and resolutions for high-contrast integral-field spectroscopy. This paper describes the design of the disperser carousel, including its mechanism architecture, optical interfaces, and associated opto-mechanical components. We present the assembly and integration approach, followed by performance measurements obtained under both ambient laboratory conditions and the instrument’s cryogenic operating temperature of 100 K.

Items.Authors: Lison Malo, Francois Wildi, Philippe Vallée, Jonathan Saint-Antoine, Sébastien Bovay, Francois Bouchy, Bachar Wehbe, Alexandre Cabral, Michael Sordet, Frédérique Baron, René Doyon, Gaspare Lo Curto, Nuno Santos
Items.Title: Design, performances, and upgrade of the thermal enclosure for the NIRPS cryogenic spectrograph at La Silla Observatory
Items.Abstract: NIRPS is a nIR, AO-assisted, high-resolution spectrograph installed on the ESO 3.6m telescope at LaSilla Observatory. Operating at 75 K, the cryogenic instrument features a fiber-fed, cross-dispersed R4 echelle design, providing simultaneous coverage of the 0.97–1.85 μm at a resolution of 80,000. In May 2023, a thermal enclosure was implemented to achieve long-term temperature stability within ±3 mK over 30 days. The enclosure was designed to be cost-effective while ensuring accessibility for preventive maintenance. However, seasonal temperature variations in the Coudé room were so significant that they required a substantial increase in the power dissipated inside the enclosure. The first upgrade, integrated an external power supply regulated by a Lakeshore 336 controller. Additionally, fans and heat exhaust components were installed to mitigate heat accumulation inside the thermal enclosure during vacuum pump operation, reducing downtime and improving overall thermal performance.

Items.Authors: G. Capobianco, G. Bergamin, A. Bemporad, S. Rasetti
Items.Title: Development and calibration of a geomagnetic disturbance measurement station
Items.Abstract: During a geomagnetic storm, as first observed by Carrington in 1859, significant electric currents are induced in the ionosphere and magnetosphere, resulting in a disturbance of the Earth’s geomagnetic field. Monitoring the Earth’s geomagnetic field is a highly effective way to track solar activity. These measurements are currently acquired in Italy by a limited network of stations managed by the INGV (National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology), located in Castello Tesino (TN), L'Aquila (AQ), Duronia (CB), and Lampedusa (AG). In the framework of SWELTO – Space WEather Laboratory in Turin Observatory, a new geomagnetic disturbance measurement station has been successfully installed and is operational at the Astrophysical Observatory of Turin since the end of 2024. This paper will detail the requirements, development, and calibration of the new station, alongside a presentation of the first measurements recorded during geomagnetic storms.

Items.Authors: Hiroshi Akitaya, Tomoki Morokuma, Koji S. Kawabata
Items.Title: Development and commissioning of the near-ultraviolet imager SCUID for the 1.5m Kanata telescope
Items.Abstract: We developed a near-ultraviolet (NUV) imager SCUID, which is capable of efficient imaging at the NUV wavelength with a field-of-view of 5 arcmin by 5 arcmin, for the 1.5m Kanata telescope at Higashi-Hiroshima Observatory in Hiroshima, Japan. The optical components and detector were carefully selected to maximize the instrument's throughput in this wavelength range. We achieve a 5-sigma detection limit of 18–19 AB mag in the u-band with a 100-sec exposure, as reported in the last conference. Recently, we have installed an instrument exchanger unit and a rotatable filter wheel at the Kanata Nasmyth focus, enabling remote operation of the instrument. The linear polarimetry module, which consists of a wiregrid polarizer and a rotatable half-wave plate, has been designed and will be installed in the instrument.

Items.Authors: Fabien Grisé, Emily Farr, Brian Fleming, Nicholas Kruczek, Briana Indahl, Kristina Davis, Kevin France, Jake McCoy, Randall McEntaffer, Stephan McCandliss
Items.Title: Development and fabrication of an EUV, ultra-low blaze angle diffraction grating for a NASA space telescope
Items.Abstract: The EUV spectral range holds critical information about million-degree  plasmas in hot white dwarf atmospheres, accretion processes, and the  interstellar medium. EUV radiation also drives atmospheric escape from  planets, making its characterization essential for assessing exoplanet  habitability around active host stars. Despite its scientific  importance, the EUV band has remained largely unexplored since NASA's  Extreme Ultraviolet Explorer (EUVE) mission that operated throughout  the 1990s, primarily due to severe interstellar extinction.  Recent advances in nanofabrication now enable a new generation of  high-efficiency diffraction gratings optimized for EUV wavelengths. We  present the design, fabrication, and characterization of an ultra-low  blaze angle diffraction grating developed for NASA's MANTIS CubeSat  mission. Our prototypes demonstrate fabrication advances that address  key technology gaps identified by NASA and support future flagship  missions including HWO.

Items.Authors: Ricardo Parra, Pierre Sansgasset, Christian Ramirez, Gerardo Smith, Tobias Müller, Steffan Lewis, Maxime Boccas, Sébastian Egner, Philippe Gitton, Dario Serrano, Jeroen Schotsaert, Sebastien Adans, Philippe Bellet, Hansjörg Weis, Robert Hyttfors, Andreas Dahl, Daniel Minzari, Torben Tang, Mikkel Østergaard Hansen, Felipe de Campos Carreri
Items.Title: Development and implementation of sustainable, large scale, industrial stripping and silver coating processes for ESO’s ELT M1
Items.Abstract: The ESO’s ELT M1 requires continuous coating renovation of 798 Zerodur segments throughout operations. This review paper presents the industrial stripping and protected silver coating processes developed to support high-volume, long-term segment maintenance. At the time of this submission, 274 segments have been coated and integrated, demonstrating process maturity and operational readiness. In addition to the process description, the paper will present statistical results from the coating of more than 300 production units, including variability across them, and long-term ageing results from qualification samples exposed and monitored for up to ten years.  The stripping process is based on a selective cerium sulfate and sulfuric acid formulation established through thermodynamic modelling and repeated exposure tests on Zerodur®. The solution removes the complete protected silver stack without measurable roughness growth across cycles and produces a stable near-surface chemistry.

Items.Authors: Laura Proserpio, Giorgia Sironi, Giovanni Pareschi, Gianpiero Tagliaferri, Michele Buzzi, Rachele Millul, Luigi Lessio, Nicola La Palombara, Salvatore Scuderi, Alessio Trois, Alida Marchetti, Carla Andreoni, Anna Maria Torricelli, Giuseppe Valsecchi, Matteo Redaelli, Fabio Zocchi, Alessandro Zanoni
Items.Title: Development and large production of the large (1.8 m) aspheric secondary mirrors for the Schwarzschild-Couder telescopes for the ASTRI and SST/CTAO air Cherenkov array via hot slumping replication
Items.Abstract: The dual-mirror aplanatic Schwarzschild–Couder (SC) design for 4 m class telescopes in the ASTRI Mini-Array and CTAO requires large, highly aspheric secondary mirrors with moderate figure and coating performance. To support over 40 SC telescopes, an industrially scalable hot-slumping process was developed to produce 1.8-meter-diameter aspheric secondaries. This includes precision mandrels, high-temperature slumpings of 20 mm float-glass, and 3D mapping metrology. The mandrel was upgraded from steel to cast iron for better accuracy and process stability. Post-slumping involves gluing mechanical pads and applying reflective coatings optimized for Cherenkov wavelengths. The results confirm that the technique meets the surface and slope error tolerances with high reproducibility. Successful fabrication of these 1.8-m monolithic secondary mirrors is a significant milestone, supporting next-gen gamma-ray astronomy, and possibly also advancing optical telescope mirror production.

Items.Authors: Fabio D'Anca, Alfonso Collura, Vincenzo Davide Cardinale, Elisa Guerriero, Claudio Saitta, Alberto Gulizzi, Andrea Meduri, Paolo Picchi, Alejandro Fernández Soler, Andrea Tozzi, Paolo Chioetto, Enzo Pascale, Antonio Scippa, Riccardo Lilli, Anna Brucalassi, Javier Pérez Álvarez, Andrea Bocchieri, Monica Rainer, Andrés García, Emanuele Pace, Paola Zuppella, Gianpaolo Preti, Luisa Sciortino, Riccardo Claudi, Giuseppe Malaguti, Marco Barbera, Michela Todaro, Ugo Lo Cicero, Salvatore Varisco, Gaspare Di Cicca, David López-García, Elisabetta Tommasi, Daniele Brienza, Manuele Gangi, Pasquale Bonfà, Angelo Olivieri, Dervis Vernani, Pierfilippo Mazzasette, Maurizio Filizzolo, Giuseppina Micela
Items.Title: Development of a cryogenic test facility for Ariel’s primary mirror
Items.Abstract: The INAF Astronomical Observatory of Palermo has adapted the XACT facility to perform cryogenic testing of the 1-meter primary mirror for ESA’s Ariel mission, which operates at about 55 K. Thermoelastic effects at this temperature require a cryogenic interferometric campaign to recover the SFE and evaluate optical behavior in a representative environment. The facility includes a 2 m × 2 m vacuum chamber with a 1.4 m entrance hatch, a closed-loop helium cryocooler, and an optical setup based on a 4D interferometer, a hexapod, and a vacuum optical window. The mirror is supported by an isostatic multi-DoF fork mount, with cooling provided through copper plates, heat shields, and thermal straps linked by an aluminum structure. Simulations show thermal gradients below 5 K and mirror temperatures below the required 100 K. The paper presents the setup, test activities, first results, and related critical issues.

Items.Authors: Raphaël Pourcelot, Thomas Bertram, Peter Bizenberger, Markus Feldt, Markus Kasper, Silvia Scheithauer, Stefan Ströbele, Horst Steuer
Items.Title: Development of an adaptive optics testbed at MPIA for the ELT/planetary camera and spectrograph (PCS)
Items.Abstract: The Planetary Camera and Spectrograph (PCS) is a proposed second-generation instrument for the European Southern Observatory (ESO) Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) aimed at direct exoplanet imaging, requiring extreme adaptive optics (AO). Building on experience from ELT/METIS as well as VLT/SPHERE adaptive optics and its upgrade SAXO+, MPIA is initiating a modular testbed to advance key AO technologies.    It will integrate two deformable mirrors, including a high-density deformable mirror prototype developed by Bertin-ALPAO in collaboration with ESO. The testbed will enable the evaluation of Fourier filtering wavefront sensors, novel mask designs, and control architectures (woofer-tweeter or independent AO stages). MPIA’s real-time control expertise enables testing of predictive and machine learning-enhanced AO strategies. In this work we present MPIA’s testbed development status and the design choices to push the extreme AO technologies for future ELT instrumentation.

Items.Authors: Jongyeob Park, Sujin Kim, Yunjong Kim, Jihun Kim, Eunsu Park, Dohoon Kim, Jung-Hwan In, Jeong-Yeol Han, Kyung-Suk Cho
Items.Title: Development of an EUV imager for the Sun-Earth L4 mission
Items.Abstract: Sun–Earth L4 observations provide a complementary 60° offset viewpoint that expands solar coverage, improves 3D characterization of coronal structures and eruptions, and enhances the overall accuracy and continuity of space weather monitoring. An EUV Imager on the L4 mission will enable global coronal monitoring, offering critical data for understanding solar eruptions and mitigating space weather impacts. Korea has established core technologies for EUV instrumentation, including precision optics, multilayer coatings, and thin-film metal filters. In addition, synchrotron-based calibration facilities have been developed to validate instrument performance across EUV wavelengths, positioning Korea with the infrastructure necessary for next-generation space observatories. This presentation will outline the scientific significance of an EUV Imager in the L4 mission, review Korea’s current technological capabilities, and present development strategies for future EUV instrumentation.

Items.Authors: Michael Sigwarth, Hemanth Pruthvi, Falk Hoffmann, Markus Roth, Falk Eilenberger, Reinhard Geiß, Stefan Schwinde, Sascha Ehrhardt, Peter Munzert, Tino Benkenstein
Items.Title: Development of large lithium niobate wafer for tunable Fabry-Pérot interferometer
Items.Abstract: For a solar full-disc imaging spectrometer with a 200-mm clear aperture solar telescope, a lithium niobate (LiNbO₃) crystal-based Fabry–Pérot interferometer with a clear aperture of 100 to 120 mm would be required. Such a wafer, polished and coated to the required specifications, has never been manufactured. Meanwhile, LiNbO₃ has become available in sizes up to eight inches, mainly for optoelectronic applications.   We present results from our initial assessment of preparing a commercial 4-inch-diameter, 250-µm-thick, Z-cut LiNbO₃ wafer for optical applications, including polishing and coating.

Items.Authors: Pablo Jiménez, Cristóbal Padilla, Jorge Jiménez
Items.Title: Development of setups for the characterisation of Novel p-on-n VLWIR Detectors
Items.Abstract: As part of the CHIPS-JU ATHENA program, new p-on-n VLWIR devices have been developed by CEA-Leti and Lynred with extended cut-off wavelengths up to 15 µm and improved operability at elevated operating temperatures. We present the commissioning and validation strategy implemented at IFAE for the experimental setups designed to support these next-generation technologies. We outline the requirements and implementation of the dedicated cryogenic and optical systems, capable of delivering controlled broadband illumination across the 0.8–15 µm range, and describe the procedures defined to verify their performance, stability, and operational readiness. Commissioning results will be presented, and a set of preliminary detector tests will be carried out to validate the performance of the setups. These activities will confirm that the systems meet the required functional specifications and are fully prepared for upcoming experimental campaigns within the ATHENA detector program.

Items.Authors: Alexander S. Kutyrev, Paul Scowen, Meng-Ping Chang, Kywoon Kim, Ming Ke, Nick Costen, Ron Hu, Eduardo Aguayo, Fred Wang, Edward Wollack, Timothy Miller, Allison Youngblood, Stephan McCandliss, Mackenzie Carlson, Emily Witt
Items.Title: Development of the next-generation microshutter arrays for the UV/visible spectroscopy
Items.Abstract: Next-generation microshutter arrays (MSA) technology is under active development to meet the demanding multiplexing and target-selection requirements of the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO). These next generation devices feature significantly larger formats compare to the previous JWST version, enhanced actuation efficiency, and improved robustness. Large-format next-generation microshutter arrays are currently in fabrication, with parallel progress on the accompanying system-level test hardware, including the vacuum chamber and the accompanying drive electronics.   In addition to the HWO development effort, small-format versions of the next-generation microshutter arrays have already demonstrated successful flight performance in the OAx-FORTIS suborbital program. A new version of the small MSA will be delivered to the next OAx-FORTIS flight, providing continued validation of the technology and a rapid path for maturing design features relevant to the large HWO-type arrays.

Items.Authors: Kantapong Tharawan, Krittapas Chanchaiworawit, Jitsupa Paenoi, Samattachai Tanun, Teerawat Kuha, Auychai Laoyang, That Chomchuen, Pakawat Prasit, Thansita Thomrungpiyathan, Pathompong Butpan, Rungrit Anutarawiramkul, Anuphong Inpan, Suchinno Kanthum, Manlika Pinkaew, Apichat Leckngam
Items.Title: Development of upgraded mechanical components for the low-resolution spectrograph (LRS) and the compact low-resolution spectrograph (CoLoRS)
Items.Abstract: We present the development of upgraded mechanical components that enhance the operational efficiency of the Low-Resolution Spectrograph (LRS) at the 2.4-m Thai National Telescope and the Compact Low-Resolution Spectrograph (CoLoRS) at the Thai Robotic Telescopes network. Key processes include installation, commissioning, verification, and on-sky operation. The LRS incorporates an ANDOR Newton 940 CCD with a new liquid-cooling system that reaches −100 °C at 60% power and maintains stable performance for 10 hours, representing a 16.8% improvement. An adjustable stage for the ZWO ASI 6200MM guiding camera enables precise focusing. For CoLoRS, a lightweight adapter with an integrated guiding shaft allows rapid installation, while FEA confirms displacement below 0.01 mm. A redesigned counterweight system improves compactness and cable management.

Items.Authors: Myung K. Cho, Hong-Suh Yim, Jaemann Kyeong, Gary Poczulp, Jung Hyun Jo, Myung-Jin Kim, Ming Liang, Ellie Hileman, Sungki Cho, Hee-Jae Lee, Youn Kil Jung, JeongAhn Youngmin, Hong-Kyu Moon
Items.Title: Development of wide field sky survey telescopes
Items.Abstract: We present a summary of the design and development for Near Space Optical Survey telescopes. This is a collaborative effort between the Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute (KASI) and the NSF’s National Optical-Infrared Astronomy Research Laboratory (NOIRLab) aiming to discover and catalog near-Earth asteroids. This sky survey optical telescope is a 1.6m primary mirror with a 5 square degree field of view, and will be installed and operated at the Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory (CTIO) in Chile. It will have a wide field corrector unit in a prime focus configuration with a set of 7 corrector lenses. The telescope design at an equatorial mount was adopted and enhanced based on the features from current Korea Microlensing Telescope Network at CTIO. This sky survey telescope will be the first dedicated observation facility for asteroid survey in the southern hemisphere in 1.6-meter class telescopes. The key optical and mechanical systems in telescope will be addressed.

Items.Authors: Tianrui Sun, Yiding Ping, Fan Li, Bin Li, Han Qu, Haibin Zhao
Items.Title: development progress and science drivers of the 4.2m ground-based astrometric telescope
Items.Abstract: Purple Mountain Observatory is building a new 4.2-meter telescope at the Lenghu B+ site in Qinghai Province, China. The 4.2-m ground-based astrometric telescope is intended to carry out follow-up observations of gamma-ray bursts and gravitational-wave events, obtain spectra of supernovae, and perform astrometric measurements of selected Solar System targets.  The telescope has one Cassegrain focus and two Nasmyth foci. The Cassegrain focus hosts the main imaging camera, which includes multiple filters and provides a field of view of approximately 10′ × 10′. The two Nasmyth ports will be equipped with a medium- to low-resolution spectrograph and an adaptive-optics camera.  This presentation will report on the development progress of the telescope and describe the range of scientific programs it is designed to support.

Items.Authors: Takafumi Kamizuka, Yuki Hirao, Akira C. Naruse, Takashi Miyata, Shigeyuki Sako, Itsuki Sakon, Kengo Tachibana, Riko Senoo, Yuki Kojima, Ichiro Jikuya, Noboru Ebizuka, Takuya Hosobata, Sunao Hasegawa, Fumihiko Usui, Ryou Ohsawa, Mizuho Uchiyama, Takashi Onaka, Hirokazu Kataza, Kotaro Kohno, Kentaro Motohara, Takeo Minezaki, Fumi Egusa, Masahiro Konishi, Hidenori Takahashi, Kazuya Matsubayashi, Hiroaki Sameshima, Kana Morokuma-Matsui, Mitsuyoshi Yamagishi, Masataka Imai, Takashi Horiuchi, Natsuko Kato, Yuzuru Yoshii
Items.Title: Development status of TAO/MIMIZUKU: performance of the long-wavelength MIR (MIR-L) channel and NIR channel upgrades
Items.Abstract: MIMIZUKU is the first-generation mid-infrared instrument for the University of Tokyo Atacama Observatory (TAO) 6.5-m telescope. TAO provides high atmospheric transmittance in the infrared including unique access to the 30-micron band (30-40 microns). MIMIZUKU covers 1.2-38 microns for imaging and low-resolution spectroscopy and enables long-term monitoring by achieving accurate atmospheric absorption correction using its Field Stacker system.  MIMIZUKU has three optical channels: NIR (1.2–5.6 microns), MIR-S (7.0–26 microns), and MIR-L (24–38 microns). Recent development has focused on the NIR and MIR-L channels. The NIR channel was upgraded with a reflective slit and grism to enhance throughput and field of view. The MIR-L channel was fully integrated and tested, incorporating a 128x128 Si:Sb array, a silicon moth-eye lens, membrane metal-mesh filters, and a cryogenic optical-path switch. We report the latest status and expected on-sky performance at TAO.

Items.Authors: Ariadna Calcines Rosario, Sarah Matthews, Hamish Reid
Items.Title: Developments on slicers in the EUV for the first EUV integral field spectrograph
Items.Abstract: The image slicer technology is widely applied in the IR, Visible and, more recently, UV spectral ranges. We present the latest developments of this technology for their first application in the Extreme Ultra-Violet (EUV) regime at 18 nm. The main challenges relate to: surface roughness, which we have reduced from 1 to 0.2 nm RMS; the novel developments on Multi-layer (M-L) dielectric coatings for two simultaneous spectral windows centred at 18 and 25 nm and the first application to slicers; and the slicer width, for which we have manufactured the thinnest slicers in the world with a width of 15 microns. The activities undertaken to increase TRL and the next steps towards achieving the space qualification will be presented. These developments are proposed for the first EUV integral field spectrograph, SISA (Spectral Imager of the Solar Atmosphere), included in the SPARK solar mission proposal selected by ESA in Step 1 for an M-class mission opportunity.

Items.Authors: Melanie Ulitschka, Enrico Hilpert, Tatjana Porwol, Luxuan Cai, Ralf Steinkopf, Sandra Müller, Mathias Rohde, Markus Unger, Robert Jende, Peter Weide, Jan Kinast, Stefan Risse
Items.Title: Direct ultra-precise processing of optical freeform RSA6061 surfaces with shape correction and smoothing techniques
Items.Abstract: Technical aluminium alloys like RSA6061 are essential for high-performance mirror devices. The surface error topography after common ultra-precise machining meet the requirements for infrared applications. However, for shorter wavelengths such as VIS or EUV, optical surface quality demands are much higher. Usually, a nickel-phosphorous (NiP) coating is needed due to the challenges of ultra-precision machining of aluminium, which often results in significant surface roughening. A promising solution for direct aluminium machining combines ion beam figuring (IBF) with chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) to effectively reduce both form errors and roughness.

Items.Authors: Ondrej Kitzler, Christian Schwab, Julian Stürmer, Jacob Pember, Dane Zielinski-Nicolson, Thorsten Fuehrer, Jonathan Crass, Gert Raskin, David Coutts
Items.Title: Doppler-free spectroscopy of the Cesium D1 line as absolute wavelength reference for the iLocater near-IR Etalon calibrator
Items.Abstract: Stabilised broadband etalons are ideal calibrators for extreme-precision radial-velocity spectrometers. Due to inherent drift, they must be referenced to an absolute frequency standard, such as an atomic absorption line. We have expanded our etalon-locking technique using saturated absorption spectroscopy of alkali atoms to the Cs D1 line at 895 nm. This wavelength lies just outside the iLocater spectral range but remains within the single-mode range of the fibers used here. Locking the etalon close to, but outside, the spectrometer bandpass avoids suppressing the atomic-probe laser and prevents its light from entering the instrument. We have built a custom ECDL at this wavelength, producing narrow-linewidth, tunable laser light. Additional saturated-absorption lines also allow probing etalon stability at multiple wavelengths; currently available in our lab are 780 nm (Rb D2), 852 nm (Cs D2), and 895 nm (Cs D1).

Items.Authors: Xana Delpueyo, José Alonso Burgal, Carlos Colodro-Conde, Pablo de Chaves, Luis Guirado-Fuentes, Juan Francisco Hernández, David Rodríguez Muñoz, José Carlos San Luis, Samuel Sordo, Alfonso Ynigo, Álex Oscoz
Items.Title: DRAGO Project: SWIR cameras for nano- and micro-satellites
Items.Abstract: IACTEC-Space is an IAC initiative for developing advanced instrumentation for small satellites dedicated to astronomy and Earth observation. One of its goal is to monitor Earth’s dynamic processes from orbit with compact, high-performance imaging systems. The first instruments, DRAGO-1 and DRAGO-2, operate in the SWIR range (1.1 µm and 1.6 µm) using an uncooled InGaAs detector based on proprietary design, unique in the market. Launched in 2021 and 2023, respectively, they enabled imaging of the 2021 La Palma eruption and the 2023 Tenerife wildfire. DRAGO-1 provides 300 m resolution, while DRAGO-2 reaches 50 m, improvable to 30 m via non-interpolated super-resolution. An upgraded DRAGO-2 is onboard ALISIO-1, the first Canarian satellite. Current developments include IACSAT ASTRO-1 and DRAGO-3, featuring four NIR/SWIR bands with ~10 m/pixel resolution, enhancing natural disaster detection within the future Canarian Earth-observation constellation.

Items.Authors: Mona El Morsy, Olivier Guyon, Barnaby Norris, Sergio Leon-Saval, Sébastien Vievard, Julien Lozi, Thayne Currie, Yoo Jung Kim, Mike Fitzgerald, Nemanja Jovanovic
Items.Title: Efficient, simultaneous exoplanet spectroscopy, wavefront control and calibration at deep contrast with hybrid mode-selective photonic lanterns
Items.Abstract: HWO aims to directly image objects orbiting Sun-like stars using a 6m telescope capable of high-contrast imaging (10^-10) and spectroscopy to search for biosignatures in habitable-zone planets. Lab and ground-based telescope projects show SMFs effectiveness to enhance spectral stability and reduce modal noise, enabling SMF-fed spectrographs in future space missions like HWO. Long integrations require precise wavefront measurement for deep contrast and robust starlight calibration. Photonic lanterns (PLs) couple light over a broader angular range, converting a multimode input into multiple single-mode outputs. At the focal plane, they act as compact wavefront sensors. The Hybrid-Mode Selective PL (HMSPL) directs planet light into a central SMF for mid-R spectroscopy while adjacent SMFs route speckle light to a low-R spectrograph, eliminating NCPA and optimizing throughput. We present HMSPL’s dual role and planned tests at UTSA's high contrast imaging lab and at SCExAO/Subaru Telescope

Items.Authors: Marco Colussi, Marco Mattietto, Leo Colussi, Gianmarco Franceschini, Andrea Fadalti, Nicola Casoni, Francesco Bevini, Pascal Martinez, Mark Wallace
Items.Title: ELT Dome project: from final design to first rotation on site
Items.Abstract: The ELT Dome, now in advanced construction and early commissioning at Cerro Armazones, combines a 90-m concrete pier with an 80-m-high rotating steel enclosure weighing about 6000 t. The hemispherical structure, equipped with slit doors providing a 42-m aperture, has completed major assembly steps and full rotation tests on its 36 trolleys. Thermal control is ensured through fire-resistant cladding, a dedicated windscreen and 89 louvers, and a custom HVAC system stabilizing the 300000 m³ chamber. The paper presents the final design and key construction and early commissioning results.

Items.Authors: Nour Skaf, Olivier Guyon, Sebastien Vievard, Elsa Huby, Sylvestre Lacour, Manon Le Teuff
Items.Title: Enabling photonic lantern high contrast imaging with DrWHO
Items.Abstract: We present a new photonic pathway toward high-contrast imaging by applying the DrWHO empirical optimization framework to a photonic lantern. Classical DrWHO implementations rely on separate science and wavefront sensors, limiting performance from several issues. Replacing the focal-plane detector with a photonic lantern feeding a single detector provides simultaneous spectral and spatial information, enabling high contrast at ~0.5l/D angular separations. In this architecture, single-mode fibers act as directional spatial filters: concentrating stellar light into one fiber makes the remaining fibers sensitive to off-axis planetary signals. DrWHO iteratively learns the WFS state that maximizes a chosen metric, either for blind searches - by driving stellar light into one fiber - or targeted detection, by optimizing the coupling of stellar and planetary flux across selected fibers. Items.Authors: Sebastian Stoebenau, Sebastian Stahringer, Frank Nürnberg, Stefan Seifried
Items.Title: Enabling the next generation of space optics: ultra-precision manufacturing for large-diameter mirrors
Items.Abstract: Advanced optical components are essential in many high-tech applications, ranging from simple aspheres to complex freeform surfaces and from microlenses to large space optics. Their production involves multiple grinding steps to form the geometry, followed by polishing to achieve optical quality and correct shape and mid-spatial-frequency errors. OptoTech, part of the Schunk Group, offers a complete portfolio for precision-optics manufacturing, including tooling, fixtures, advanced grinding and polishing machines, and production monitoring systems. Recent developments include the UPG 500 CNC and UPG 1000 CNC machining centers for large-scale optics, delivering high shape accuracy and minimal sub-surface damage. Combined with OptoTech’s advanced polishing processes, these technologies reduce production time and ensure a fast return on investment.

Items.Authors: Elvio Hernández Suárez, Dylan Carroll, Haroldo Lorenzo Hernández, Iñigo Arizaga, Enrique Joven, Javier De Miguel-Hernández
Items.Title: Engineering challenges in the integration of the DALI cryogenic dark-matter prototype
Items.Abstract: The Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias (IAC) is developing the DALI (Dark-photons & Axion-Like particles Interferometer) Proof-of-Principle prototype, an astroparticle instrument conceived to probe axions and dark photons in the 6–60 GHz range. This paper describes the engineering development of the prototype, with particular emphasis on the mechanical integration of a 72-magnet array into a ferromagnetic yoke and on the thermal architecture required to cool a 350 kg magnetic assembly to cryogenic temperatures. During assembly, magnetic instabilities not anticipated in the nominal design were identified, leading to the implementation of dedicated tooling, safety procedures, and supplementary retention systems. Cryo-vacuum tests of the fully integrated system demonstrated stable operation under combined magnetic, vacuum, and cryogenic conditions, reaching approximately 37 K in the magnetic assembly and 10 K in thermally isolated detector components.

Items.Authors: Douglas Miller, Greg Taylor, Jennifer Power, Sam Ragland
Items.Title: Enhanced seeing mode at the Large Binocular Telescope Observatory: a comparison with ground layer AO
Items.Abstract: The SOUL Adaptive Optics System at the Large Binocular Telescope Observatory (LBTO), in conjunction with the f/30 camera on the LUCI (LBT Utility Camera in the Infrared) instruments, delivers diffraction-limited image quality with a 30”x30” field of view. The AO system includes a low-mode form delivering only 10 modes of correction (tip, tilt, focus, 2 × astigmatism, 2 × coma, 2 × trefoil and spherical) to remove jitter and residual aberrations. This low-mode form of operation is referred to as Enhanced Seeing mode (ESM) and is found to consistently provide significant angular resolution across the full 4’x4’ field of view of the wide field f/N3.75 camera on the LUCI instruments. In this paper we will show the results of simulations which will compare ESM to Ground Layer AO (GLAO). We will also compare ESM data with engineering data taken with the ARGOS GLAO system. We intend to demonstrate the superb quality of ESM observations at the LBTO.

Items.Authors: Thomas Procter, Glenn Walters, Megan Dubay, Nicholas Law, Jonathan Carney, Hank Corbett, James Dockery, Katie M. Fasbender, Shannon Fitton, Lawrence Machia, William Marshall, Donovan Schlekat, Alan Vasquez Soto, Jonah L. Aponte, Alex Bucheli, Thomas Cowart, Colin H. Grimes, Amy S. Ishiguro, Michael Ronco
Items.Title: Environmental isolation for the Argus Array: comparative analysis of air curtains and glass windows
Items.Abstract: The Argus Array utilizes a unique pseudo-focal design to allow multiple optical tube assemblies to observe through a single, shared oculus. This configuration allows the telescope enclosure to be sealed for enhanced stability. Using Python and scripted-simulations in Zemax OpticStudio, we analyze oculus sizing and vignetting limits for the Array. Furthermore, we compare the viability of a large fused silica window against an air curtain system, centering our findings around vignetting, ghosting, transmission, point spread function performance, and the collective effect on limiting magnitude.

Items.Authors: Erica E. Lugo-Ibarra, Laurence Sabin, Wen-Ping Chen, Yair Krongold, David Hiriart Garcia, Liliana Figueroa Carrillo, Alfonso H. Franco, Joel V. Herrera-Vazquez, Eduardo Lopez Angeles, Francisco Javier Valenzuela Vargas, Gerardo Sierra Díaz, Fernando Quiros, Eduardo Lopez Angeles, Yi Chou, Chow-Choong Ngeow, Yen-Chen Pan, Ming-Hsin Chang, Anli Tsai, Yung-Hsin Chang, Lung-Ting Wang, Javier Alonso Hernandez Landa, Julio Ramirez, Jesús González
Items.Title: Environmental site characterization for the remote operation of the TransPacific 2m telescope (T P2m) at the San Pedro Mártir Observatory (OAN-SPM), Baja California, Mexico
Items.Abstract: This work presents the environmental site characterization conducted to support the implementation and remote operation of the TransPacific 2m Telescope (TP2m) at the San Pedro Mártir Observatory (OAN-SPM), Baja California, Mexico. The TP2m project, a collaborative initiative between the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM), the National Central University (Taiwan), and international partners, will establish a new optical facility within the Sierra de San Pedro Mártir National Park. Candidate locations within the observatory were evaluated through analyses of environmental conditions, infrastructure availability, accessibility, operational requirements, and compliance with applicable environmental regulations. The selected site provides suitable conditions for remote telescope operation while minimizing vegetation removal and ecological disturbance. OAN-SPM's existing infrastructure, including electrical power, communications, access roads, and technical support facilities,

Items.Authors: Faustine Cantalloube, Olivier Absil, Valentin Christiaens, Marc Van Droogenbroeck, Carles Cantero Mitjans, Anthony Cioppa, Antoine Alaguero, Briley Lewis, Claudia Toci, Félix Sauvourel, Iain Hammond, Johan Mazoyer, Markus Bonse, Nitya Pandey, Matthias Samland, Sebastien Pierard, Sandrine Juillard
Items.Title: Exoplanet imaging data challenge phase 3: imaging circumplanetary disks
Items.Abstract: Advanced high-contrast image processing techniques are an essential ingredient making it possible to unveil faint circumstellar signals. Launched in 2019, the Exoplanet Imaging Data Challenge is a community-wide effort that offers a platform to fairly compare the latest algorithms developed over the past 20 years. After a first phase focused on the detection of point sources (exoplanets), then a second phase focused on the characterization of point sources (astrometry and spectro-photometry), the working group is preparing a third phase focused on extended source imaging. In this third phase, we will provide the community with a curated ensemble of high-contrast data set in which we injected synthetic circumstellar disks, as well as forming planets within. The morphologies and flux distributions of the injected synthetic disks are representative of the diversity of observed disks thus far thanks to high-contrast imaging instruments.

Items.Authors: Jean-Philippe Amans
Items.Title: Exorcist: suppression of fibre-interface back-reflections in astronomical spectrographs: the ghost image killer
Items.Abstract: We present EXORCIST, a simple and practical solution that is compatible with standard fibre mounting, polishing processes and which significantly reduces back-reflections at the fibre interface. The approach enables substantial suppression of ghost images while preserving mechanical robustness and manufacturability. This solution is particularly relevant for fibre-fed spectrograph requiring high contrast and low stray-light performance.  EXORCIST : the ghost image killer !

Items.Authors: B. Vasilescu, P. Piron, F. Schmutz, R. Snel, E. Di Iorio, J. Loicq
Items.Title: Experimental validation of a versatile method for full Stokes spectropolarimetry
Items.Abstract: The capacity to measure the polarization state of light is crucial for fields ranging from astronomy to biomedical imaging. However, a significant gap exists in instrumentation for compact, robust spectropolarimeters that can perform complete, snapshot measurements across a broad waveband. It is a gap that primarily affects sectors operating in harsh environments, such as the space sector. To address this, we developed a novel spectropolarimeter architecture centred on a set of three birefringent prisms. This core component enables high-fidelity, hyperspectral polarization imaging in a single shot. Experimental validation of a laboratory demonstrator confirms the technology's viability, with performance characterization at multiple wavelengths demonstrating accurate polarization recovery. This presentation outlines the instrument's operational principles, calibration methodology, and demodulation processes, laying the foundation for future miniaturized polarimetric systems.

Items.Authors: Prasanna G. Deshmukh, Gracia G., Phanindra D.V.S., Tsewang Stanzin, Sonam Jorphail, Tashi Thsering Mahay, Tsewang Gyalson, Tsewang Dorjai, Amit Kumar, Dorje Angchuk, Ramya Anche
Items.Title: Experimental vibration analysis of the 2m Himalayan Chandra Telescope for control system development
Items.Abstract: In this paper, we present results from a dedicated vibration measurement campaign on the 2-m Himalayan Chandra Telescope conducted in August 2025 using high-sensitivity accelerometers and a custom-built, high-speed data logger. The accelerometer sensors were installed at structurally significant places on the telescope to capture broadband and transient disturbances caused by the structure, axis motion, wind loading, and other subsystems. By high-rate measurements, we were able to extract the vibration spectra, modal characteristics, coherence between structural components, and temporal evolution under tracking and slewing, which directly impact pointing stability and wave-front quality. The findings provide an essential input for optimising the HCT control system architecture and improving the vibration rejection performance. The experiment has also validated the importance of incorporating these vibration sensors as a monitoring and diagnostics system with the HCT control system.

Items.Authors: Joseph W. Barrow, Jon S. Lawrence, Aaron Omadutt, Roelof S. de Jong, Suryansh Saxena
Items.Title: Exploration of small footprint stick-slip piezoelectric actuators for use in the FLEX fibre positioner system for the Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope (WST)
Items.Abstract: This work presents a novel stick-slip piezoelectric actuator for the FLEX fibre positioner, addressing the challenge of reducing footprint while maintaining precision in next-generation multi-object spectroscopic instruments such as the Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope (WST). The actuator combines compact geometry (3.2 mm diameter, 70 mm length) with high-resolution incremental motion, low power consumption, and high reliability. Three actuators can be integrated into a sub 7 mm diameter circle, enabling a simplified, single-plane assembly. This design offers a promising solution for miniaturized, accurate fibre positioning in wide-field spectroscopic applications.

Items.Authors: Younes Chahid, Tassos Aretos, Will Cochrane, Katherine Morris, David Isherwood, Zeshan Ali, Graham Wilks, Noah Schwartz, Anmol Goyal, Marcell Westsik, Alastair Macleod, Steve Watson, Anjali Bhatt, David Lunney, Bradley Frank
Items.Title: Exploring generative design AI tools for a CubeSat chassis
Items.Abstract: Generative design artificial intelligence (AI) tools are currently used in multiple scientific fields, yet their adoption in mechanical engineering computer-aided design (CAD) remains limited due to a lack of disseminated case studies, limited availability of accessible tools, insufficient training in CAD data, and the absence of universal editable file formats.     Mechanical design for astronomical instrumentation faces increasing complexity in thermal, vibrational, and mechanical requirements alongside tight project deadlines. This paper presents a practical evaluation of Autodesk Fusion generative design capabilities applied to chassis design for the ADOT CubeSat mission. Our analysis establishes clear criteria for determining when generative design tools become advantageous over traditional CAD approaches, considering component criticality, available manufacturing methods, design complexity, and part constraints.

Items.Authors: Theodore A. Grosson, Deborah Lokhorst, Alan W. McConnachie
Items.Title: Exploring the trade-space of distributed aperture telescopes in spectroscopy
Items.Abstract: Scientific programs targeting the faintest objects push modern telescopes to increasingly large apertures, high costs and complex designs. For observations in which high angular resolution is not necessary, an innovative, cheaper strategy is to use many small telescopes in place of a single large aperture, as demonstrated by instruments such as the Dragonfly Telephoto Array, the Huntsman Telescope, and the Condor Array Telescope. In this work, we discuss the merits of "distributed aperture telescopes" as applied to the use case of spectroscopic observations of ultra-diffuse galaxies (UDGs). We compare the cost and simulated scientific performance of different configurations of apertures, detectors, and other components for this purpose, finding that an array of half-metre telescopes can obtain comparable observations to large telescopes for a fraction of the cost. Finally, we discuss the path to prototyping an array which will enable a spectroscopic survey of UDGs.

Items.Authors: Manuel A. Quijada, Javier G. Del Hoyo, Luis V. Rodriguez de Marcos, Breann N. Sitarski, Edward J. Wollack, Andrew W. Howe, David R. Boris, Scott G. Walton, Mateo Batkis, John J. Hennessy
Items.Title: Exposure of highly reflective far-ultraviolet coatings to LEO environment for TRL advancement for the Habitable Worlds Observatory
Items.Abstract: Recent developments in performing aluminum (Al) coatings protected with different F-based overcoats offer unprecedented reflectance performance in the FUV in addition to improved environmental stability. These new coating technologies result from collaborations between the Goddard Space Flight Center and two other institutions (NRL and JPL). In this paper, we report on environmental/material property characterization of several of these new Al-based FUV coatings before and after they were flown for 6 months in the International Space Station during the Materials International Space Station Experiment-20th experiment (MISSE-20) to advance the TRL for these mirror coating technologies.

Items.Authors: James P. Hamilton, Nicholas J. Baker, Noah R. Milder
Items.Title: Extended lifetime astronomical metal mirror coatings: maintain reflectivity and 100x reduction in pinholes using polymer cleaning before metal coating
Items.Abstract: Pinholes in metallic mirror coatings increase scatter, permit unwanted transmission, and act as initiation sites for under-film corrosion and adhesion loss. Pinhole formation is strongly influenced by substrate and chamber cleanliness and by particulate spatter during deposition. Here we present measurements from a precision pinhole-quantification instrument developed to characterize sputtered and PVD-deposited metal mirrors. Applying an Apply-Dry-Peel First Contact polymer treatment to substrates prior to deposition produced a dramatic reduction in pinhole density and a marked increase in film adhesion. Across multiple metals (Al, Au, Cr, Ag), aluminum showed the largest improvement, with pinhole counts reduced by nearly two orders of magnitude relative to untreated controls; in some treated samples, pinholes were not detected within our measurement limits. The combination of improved adhesion and reduced defect-site density suggests a path to more robust aluminum mirror coatings.

Items.Authors: Ana Iglesias Moreno, Paloma López Reyes, Alejandro García Cañas, Carlos Honrado Benítez, Nuria Gutierrez Luna, Beatriz Galiana, Sofía Julve, Guillermo López-Reyes, Francesc Valls Vicent, María Frutos Pastor, Ana Inés Gómez de Castro, Juan Ignacio Larruquert
Items.Title: Extra-narrowband FUV mirrors: robustness and performance under simulated space conditions
Items.Abstract: Far UV band-pass filters have been identified by NASA as a high-priority technological gap. Conventional narrowband reflective filters typically achieve bandwidths of ~20 nm. Yet, narrower FUV filters are demanded for future observatories requiring the detection of specific spectral lines, such as the Observatorio Ultravioleta Lunar (OUL/UCM).  Ultra-narrowband filters with ~4 nm bandwidth (FWHM), peak reflectance >70%, tunable in the 120-200-nm range have been recently developed at GOLD-FOTION. They consist in AlF₃/MgF₂ multilayer coatings. We’ll present these filters along with their increased maturation level (TRL) for space instrumentation. The filters were tested for thermal cycling, gamma radiation, and humidity. The filters remained mostly unaffected by these tests. This demonstrates their robustness, that points to a TRL 5 towards their use in space environments. This supports their potential for next-generation FUV observatories such as OUL.

Items.Authors: Savitha M. S., Nagaraju K., Raveena Khan, Mohammed H. Modi, P. K. Yadav, R. K. Gupta
Items.Title: Extreme ultraviolet polarimeter optics based on metal coatings
Items.Abstract: The Hanle effect in Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) spectral lines offers a promising diagnostic for probing the coronal vector magnetic field, but requires precise polarization measurements, yet no EUV spectropolarimeter has been operational for solar coronal observation. Reflection-based polarizers offer a way to achieve high polarization power and throughput in the EUV waveband by suitably selecting the coating materials. The simulation and experimental results demonstrate that metallic coatings such as platinum give 85–90% polarization power and more than 30% throughput across 400 - 1000 Å. These metallic-coated mirrors can be effectively incorporated into the polarimeter by optimizing the telescope optics with dielectric coatings that are transparent to visible and IR light and that effectively reflect the EUV light into the polarimeter.

Items.Authors: David Schiminovich
Items.Title: Extremely wide-field, multi-object, high-resolution spectrograph designs for future large aperture, diffraction-limited far- and near-ultraviolet space missions
Items.Abstract: A key systems-engineering challenge for future large-aperture UV space telescopes is enabling high-resolution UV spectroscopy of sparse targets distributed across wide fields. Current Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) concepts employ IFU microshutters or slicers with fields of regard of only a few arcminutes or tens of arcseconds, limiting true multiplexing of rare bright QSOs needed for high-S/N absorption-line studies. We present several wide-field patrol architectures capable of accessing the full HWO focal plane, including all-reflective and catadioptric relays, UV-transmitting fiber approaches, and advanced microshutter configurations. These concepts route light from ~20–25 targets into a single high-resolution UV spectrograph or a distributed array of compact mini-spectrographs. We assess optical performance, mechanical complexity, and interface requirements, and outline a practical development path with ground-based on-sky demonstrations.

Items.Authors: Woong-Seob Jeong, Youngsoo Jo, Yujin Yang, Myung Sang Huh, Gil Jae Lee, Jeonghyun Pyo
Items.Title: Fabrication and evaluation of aluminum image slicers for a high-throughput IFU spectrograph
Items.Abstract: We present the development and of aluminum image slicers intended for use in astronomical spectrographs. The image slicer is fabricated from aluminum materials using a diamond-turning machine equipped with customized end mills. Machining parameters were optimized through test cuts on aluminum materials, establishing stable mirror-finish conditions with an average surface roughness of ~10 nm. After optimization for prototype slicers, we achieved average surface roughness values of 10-13 nm, demonstrating reproducible smooth surfaces over the full array of slicer facets. These results confirm that direct diamond-turning machining of RSA6061 can meet the surface quality required for high-throughput, low-scatter reflective image slicers. We outline the planned integration of the fabricated image slicer into a prototype Integral-Field-Unit (IFU) spectrograph and discuss the expected improvement in observing efficiency for future ground-based and space-based instruments.

Items.Authors: Ceiwynn C. Longworth, Megan M. Delamer, Suvrath Mahadevan, Joe P. Ninan, Kathleen Gehoski, Krushna Jadhav
Items.Title: Fabrication of focusing optics for TA-MOONS: Micro-MOONS
Items.Abstract: Tackling open problems in star formation requires precise spectroscopic observations of a large number of young stellar objects, spanning a wide wavelength band from the optical through the near-infrared. The TIFR-ARIES Multi-Object Optical to Near-infrared Spectrometer (TA-MOONS) is a new astronomical instrument designed to survey young stars. To precisely position starlight into its 8 robotic arms, an array of microscopic, concave mirrors is needed. The fabrication of the mirror array called Micro-MOONS was done using two-photon polymerization 3D printing. The mirrors are created of IP-S photoresist on a silicon substrate, with fabrication focusing on uniformity, minimizing surface roughness, and preserving the desired curvature radius.
